articleTitle: On-load tap-changers current experience and future development: Users experience and perspective
publicationTitle: IEE European Seminar on Developments On-Load Tapchangers: Current Experience and Future
abstract: On-load tap-changers may represent only 5-100 % of the capital cost of a supergrid power transformer yet their operational performance and reliability is critical to realising the full asset life of the transformer. In addition, tap-changer inspections largely govern the frequency and duration of transformer circuit outages and represent a high proportion of transformer maintenance costs. This paper presents a summary of the National Grid Company's (UK) experience in such tap-changers in recent years. This experience, the changes in specification and the user-supplier relationships described are believed to be representative of a major electric utility.

publicationTitle: IEE European Seminar on Developments On-Load Tapchangers: Current Experience and Future
abstract: A power transformer is a static piece of electrical equipment and this may be a contributing factor behind its widely acknowledged reliability. Very often, it is equipped with an on-load tap-changer that has moving parts and creates electric arcs, by the very nature of its purpose. The tap-changer, therefore, presents a somewhat greater risk than the core and windings, the oil and the tank. Tap-changer technology has striven to increase integrity, reduce lifetime costs, and increase reliability and availability, by concentrating on quality. This paper describes how the transformer designer is seeking a "quality" manufacturer, with a well-proven product, at a competitive price that will attract the prospective transformer purchaser. The present day product, if obtained from reputable suppliers, goes far in meeting the ideal, but further developments are, and will always be, essential in the interests of product improvement. Transformer manufacturers, in accord with the tap-changer users, eagerly await those developments. They do, however, hope that heed is taken of their concerns in respect of dielectric proving, by the specification writers.

articleTitle: On-load tap-changers current experience and future developments. Principles and resulting benefits of separate tank (external) tap-changers
publicationTitle: IEE European Seminar on Developments On-Load Tapchangers: Current Experience and Future
abstract: This paper deals with three types of high speed resistor on-load tap-changers designed to be mounted on the side or end of power transformers. These include double compartment tap-changers with separate selector and diverter compartments, single compartment selector tap-changers and in-tank tap-changers with barrier boards. The major advantage of separate tank tap-changers is their easy access for inspection and maintenance, making them particularly suitable for the user to service.

articleTitle: European seminar "On-load tap changers current experience and future developments"
publicationTitle: IEE European Seminar on Developments On-Load Tapchangers: Current Experience and Future
abstract: This paper examines the high-speed resistor tap changers installed inside power transformer tanks. In-tank tap changers are designed to match the specific requirements of electric utility companies as well as transformer manufacturers concerning the number of positions, voltage stress across the tap winding, insulation to ground and so on. This large variety is possible due to the modular design concept employed.
